title: Margherita Pizza
description: A hot oven and restraint are the whole trick — San Marzano tomatoes crushed by hand, fresh mozzarella torn (never sliced), and basil added after the bake so it stays green.

image.alt: Close-up of a pizza baking in a dark oven, dramatic golden light

ingredients: 500g pizza dough (store-bought or homemade), at room temperature
200g canned San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand, drained of excess liquid
250g fresh mozzarella, torn into rough pieces and blotted dry
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for finishing
A handful of fresh basil leaves
steps: Put a pizza stone or heavy baking sheet in the oven and preheat to its highest setting (250–290°C) for at least 45 minutes.
Stir the garlic and a pinch of salt into the crushed tomatoes; don't cook the sauce — it finishes in the oven.
Stretch the dough on a semolina-dusted surface into a 30cm round, working from the center out and leaving a puffier rim.
Spread the tomato sauce thinly, leaving a 2cm border. Scatter the torn mozzarella evenly.
Slide the pizza onto the hot stone. Bake 6–9 minutes, until the crust is blistered and the cheese is bubbling with brown spots.
Remove, drizzle with olive oil, scatter basil leaves, and slice immediately.
note: Blot the mozzarella dry before topping — wet cheese steams instead of browning and leaves the crust soggy.
